chunks: And 'Asim narrated from Abu Basir, who said:

I asked him about a male slave and a female slave who are emancipated by tadbir. He said: The master may make a mukatabah contract with him if he wishes, and he does not have the right to sell him unless the slave wishes that he sell him during the term of his life. And he may take his property if he has property.

key_terms.الْأَمَةِ: the female slave under discussion in the ruling
key_terms.الْعَبْدِ: the male slave under discussion in the ruling
key_terms.عَنْ دُبُرٍ: through posthumous emancipation, meaning freedom linked to the master's death
key_terms.لِمَوْلَاهُ: for his master; indicating the legal authority of the owner in this matter
key_terms.مَالٌ: property or wealth possessed by the slave
key_terms.مُدَّةَ حَيَاتِهِ: for the duration of his lifetime
key_terms.يُكَاتِبَهُ: to enter into a mukatabah contract for emancipation in exchange for payment

ai.seo_question: What are the legal rulings on selling or contracting emancipation for a mudabbar slave in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives fiqh rulings concerning a mudabbar slave, one whose emancipation is tied to the master's death. It states that the master may contract mukatabah with such a slave, may not sell the slave without the slave's consent during his lifetime, and may take the slave's wealth if the slave possesses wealth.
